title: S 29 (120th General Assembly): Voting identification
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id) not stated.
(b_no_id_remedy)
(section) SECTION 1 (amends 7-13-710(D)(1)(a), religious objection)
(quote) he may complete a written statement under penalty of perjury at the polling place and affirm that the elector: (i) is the same individual who personally appeared at the polling place; (ii) cast the provisional ballot on election day; and (iii) has a religious objection to being photographed.
(section) SECTION 1 (amends 7-13-710(D)(1)(a))
(quote) Upon completion of the written statement, which must be signed by the elector, the elector may cast a provisional ballot.
(section) SECTION 1 (amends 7-13-710(D)(1)(b), reasonable impediment)
(quote) he may complete a written statement, which must be signed by the elector, under the penalty of perjury at the polling place and affirm that the elector: (i) is the same individual who personally appeared at the polling place; (ii) cast the provisional ballot on election day; and (iii) the elector suffers from a reasonable impediment that prevents him from obtaining photograph identification.
(section) SECTION 1 (amends 7-13-710(D)(2))
(quote) If the county board of registration and elections determines that the voter was challenged only for the inability to provide proof of identification and the required written statement is submitted, the county board of registration and elections shall find that the provisional ballot is valid unless the board has grounds to believe the written statement is false.
(c_mail_ballot_id) not stated.
(d_proof_of_citizenship) not stated.
(e_other_rule) not stated.
(other) SECTION 1 reprints all of 7-13-710 (A)-(E) as 'amended to read'; only the affidavit-to-written-statement words are marked new.
(other) SECTION 2: takes effect on preclearance by the U.S. Department of Justice or a declaratory judgment of the D.C. federal district court, whichever comes first.
(other) version: 2012-12-13_Introduced (only version): replaces 'affidavit' with 'written statement' in the religious-objection and reasonable-impediment provisional-ballot procedures, and requires the elector to sign the statement.
(other) note: Slot a is 'not stated': the whole 7-13-710 is reprinted, including the unchanged ID list in (A) (driver's license, DMV photo ID, passport, military photo ID, voter registration card with photo, all valid and current) and the unchanged provisional-ballot rule in (C), but none of that is marked new. Whether the reprint matches the law as it stood after Act 27 of 2011 was not checked against any other source. The strike/new markers are clear in this file. One version.
(note) Off this topic: the bill sets no ID or citizenship-proof rule.
